name: Sepia photograph

influenced_by: 19th-century photographic toning chemistry (using sepia, a pigment from cuttlefish ink)

garments: not a fashion look — a photographic toning process
reacts_against: nothing — sepia toning was originally a practical choice (it made prints more chemically stable and resistant to fading, not just a stylistic one), later becoming visual shorthand for "old photograph" or "the past" once black-and-white and color film made it unnecessary.
revivals: a default "nostalgic" filter in nearly every photo-editing app

findings: dark — about 52% of the measured color across 6 Commons photos is below mid-lightness
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Wikimedia Commons images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
